name.text: Finding the mistake in choosing a probability law

questiontext.text:
A fair die is rolled and a fair spinner numbered 1 to \({@s@}\) is spun. Baraka wrote three probabilities. Exactly one line is wrong.

Line 1: [[if test="is(ord[1]=1)"]]\(P(\text{die shows } {@a@} \text{ and spinner shows } {@b@}) = [[if test="is(er=1)"]]\dfrac{1}{6} + \dfrac{1}{{@s@}} = {@1/6+1/s@}[[else]]\dfrac{1}{6} \times \dfrac{1}{{@s@}} = {@1/(6*s)@}[[/if]]\)[[elif test="is(ord[1]=2)"]]\(P(\text{die shows } {@a@} \text{ or } {@c@}) = [[if test="is(er=2)"]]\dfrac{1}{6} \times \dfrac{1}{6} = \dfrac{1}{36}[[else]]\dfrac{1}{6} + \dfrac{1}{6} = \dfrac{1}{3}[[/if]]\)[[else]]\(P(\text{die shows } {@a@} \text{ or spinner shows } {@b@}) = [[if test="is(er=3)"]]\dfrac{1}{6} + \dfrac{1}{{@s@}} = {@1/6+1/s@}[[else]]1 - \dfrac{5}{6} \times \dfrac{{@s-1@}}{{@s@}} = {@(s+5)/(6*s)@}[[/if]]\)[[/if]]

Line 2: [[if test="is(ord[2]=1)"]]\(P(\text{die shows } {@a@} \text{ and spinner shows } {@b@}) = [[if test="is(er=1)"]]\dfrac{1}{6} + \dfrac{1}{{@s@}} = {@1/6+1/s@}[[else]]\dfrac{1}{6} \times \dfrac{1}{{@s@}} = {@1/(6*s)@}[[/if]]\)[[elif test="is(ord[2]=2)"]]\(P(\text{die shows } {@a@} \text{ or } {@c@}) = [[if test="is(er=2)"]]\dfrac{1}{6} \times \dfrac{1}{6} = \dfrac{1}{36}[[else]]\dfrac{1}{6} + \dfrac{1}{6} = \dfrac{1}{3}[[/if]]\)[[else]]\(P(\text{die shows } {@a@} \text{ or spinner shows } {@b@}) = [[if test="is(er=3)"]]\dfrac{1}{6} + \dfrac{1}{{@s@}} = {@1/6+1/s@}[[else]]1 - \dfrac{5}{6} \times \dfrac{{@s-1@}}{{@s@}} = {@(s+5)/(6*s)@}[[/if]]\)[[/if]]

Line 3: [[if test="is(ord[3]=1)"]]\(P(\text{die shows } {@a@} \text{ and spinner shows } {@b@}) = [[if test="is(er=1)"]]\dfrac{1}{6} + \dfrac{1}{{@s@}} = {@1/6+1/s@}[[else]]\dfrac{1}{6} \times \dfrac{1}{{@s@}} = {@1/(6*s)@}[[/if]]\)[[elif test="is(ord[3]=2)"]]\(P(\text{die shows } {@a@} \text{ or } {@c@}) = [[if test="is(er=2)"]]\dfrac{1}{6} \times \dfrac{1}{6} = \dfrac{1}{36}[[else]]\dfrac{1}{6} + \dfrac{1}{6} = \dfrac{1}{3}[[/if]]\)[[else]]\(P(\text{die shows } {@a@} \text{ or spinner shows } {@b@}) = [[if test="is(er=3)"]]\dfrac{1}{6} + \dfrac{1}{{@s@}} = {@1/6+1/s@}[[else]]1 - \dfrac{5}{6} \times \dfrac{{@s-1@}}{{@s@}} = {@(s+5)/(6*s)@}[[/if]]\)[[/if]]

Give each probability exactly, as a fraction or an exact decimal.

(a) Which line is wrong?

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) What is the mistake?

[[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

(c) Give the correct probability for that line.

[[input:ans3]] [[validation:ans3]] [[feedback:prt3]]

generalfeedback.text:
Check each line. For and with the die and the spinner, which are separate experiments, multiply. For or with one die, the two numbers cannot both happen, so add. For or with the die and the spinner, both can happen together, so use \(1 - P(\text{neither})\).

[[if test="is(er=1)"]]

(a) Line {@wp@} adds for an and event. (b) The die and the spinner are independent and both must happen, so multiply. (c) \(\dfrac{1}{6} \times \dfrac{1}{{@s@}} = {@ta3@}\).

[[elif test="is(er=2)"]]

(a) Line {@wp@} multiplies for an or event on one die. (b) The die cannot show {@a@} and {@c@} at once, so add. (c) \(\dfrac{1}{6} + \dfrac{1}{6} = \dfrac{1}{3}\).

[[else]]

(a) Line {@wp@} adds two events that can happen together. (b) The outcome where the die shows {@a@} and the spinner shows {@b@} is counted twice. (c) \(1 - P(\text{neither}) = 1 - \dfrac{5}{6} \times \dfrac{{@s-1@}}{{@s@}} = {@ta3@}\).

[[/if]]

Check the other lines.

truefeedback.text: Adding is right for mutually exclusive events (Line {@mel@}).

falsefeedback.text: Your reason describes a different mistake. Ask: is the line about and or or, and can the two events happen together?

truefeedback.text: Your value is close to the right one but has been rounded. Give the exact probability as a fraction or an exact decimal.
That is Baraka's value, which contains the mistake.
A probability is always between 0 and 1, so \({@ans3@}\) cannot be a probability.

falsefeedback.text: Use the right law for that line: multiply for and with separate experiments; add for or when both cannot happen; otherwise use \(1 - P(\text{neither})\).
